name: Cairo
operatingHours: Cairo Metro (Lines 1, 2 and 3) runs ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM daily, to ~2:00 AM during Ramadan. Trains every ~3–6 min at peak, longer late evening. Each train has women-only carriages (usually the middle cars). Line 4 to Giza is under construction (planned 2028).
fareInfo: Fares depend on the number of stations (from 27 March 2026): up to 9 stations EGP 10, up to 16 EGP 12, up to 23 EGP 15, more than 23 EGP 20. Buy a single magnetic ticket at the station window for each trip; stored-value and subscription cards are also sold. No metro serves the airport or the Pyramids.

lines.name: Metro Line 3
stations: El-Dabaa Axis Metro Station (Rod El-Farag Axis)

sights.name: Egyptian Museum
sights.note: The pink neoclassical museum on Tahrir Square holding the world's largest collection of pharaonic antiquities; many Tutankhamun pieces have moved to the Grand Egyptian Museum, but the halls remain packed with statues, coffins and papyri.

sights.name: Khan el-Khalili
sights.note: The medieval bazaar of Islamic Cairo, a warren of lanes selling brass lamps, spices, perfume and silver, with the historic El Fishawy café at its edge.
sights.hours: Most shops ~10:00 AM–~11:00 PM; quieter Sunday mornings

sights.name: Sharia al-Muizz
sights.note: The main street of Fatimid Cairo, a pedestrianised stretch of mosques, madrasas and Mamluk mansions such as the Qalawun complex, especially atmospheric when lit at night.
sights.hours: Open street; individual monuments ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
sights.note: Founded in 970, one of the oldest mosques in Cairo and the seat of Al-Azhar University, with a broad marble courtyard and five minarets from different eras.
sights.hours: Visits ~9:00 AM–~9:00 PM outside prayer times; modest dress, headscarves for women

sights.name: Al-Azhar Park
sights.note: A landscaped hilltop park built on a former rubbish mound, with fountains, gardens, a lakeside café and views over the minarets of Islamic Cairo to the Citadel.

sights.name: Citadel of Saladin & Mosque of Muhammad Ali
sights.note: Saladin's 12th-century hilltop fortress, crowned by the Ottoman-style Alabaster Mosque of Muhammad Ali, with terraces looking over the whole city.

sights.name: Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hassan
sights.note: A huge 14th-century Mamluk mosque and school below the Citadel, with soaring iwans around a central courtyard; the Al-Rifai Mosque stands directly opposite.

sights.name: Mosque of Ibn Tulun
sights.note: Cairo's oldest intact mosque (879), a vast arcaded courtyard with an unusual spiral-staired minaret; the Gayer-Anderson Museum adjoins it.

sights.name: Museum of Islamic Art
sights.note: One of the largest Islamic art collections anywhere, with ceramics, woodwork, metalwork and manuscripts from across the Islamic world.

sights.name: The Hanging Church
sights.note: Cairo's best-known Coptic church, built above the gatehouse of the Roman Babylon Fortress and reached by a stair from the street, in the Coptic quarter of Old Cairo.

sights.name: Coptic Museum
sights.note: The world's largest collection of Coptic Christian art, from textiles and icons to carved wood and early manuscripts, inside the old Roman fortress walls.

sights.name: National Museum of Egyptian Civilization
sights.note: A modern museum in Fustat tracing Egypt from prehistory to today; its underground Royal Mummies Hall displays the pharaohs moved here in 2021.

sights.name: Cave Church (Monastery of St. Simon)
sights.note: A cluster of churches carved into the Mokattam cliffs above Manshiyat Naser, including an amphitheatre-like main church seating thousands.

sights.name: Manial Palace
sights.note: The early-20th-century palace of Prince Mohamed Ali Tewfik on Roda Island, mixing Ottoman, Moorish and Persian styles amid banyan-shaded gardens.

sights.name: Cairo Tower
sights.note: A 187 m lattice-patterned tower on Gezira Island from 1961, with an open-air observation deck over the Nile and, on clear days, the Pyramids.

sights.name: Pyramids of Giza
sights.note: The last surviving wonder of the ancient world: the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure and the Great Sphinx on the desert plateau, ~18 km southwest of Tahrir (listed under Giza on TripAdvisor).

sights.name: Grand Egyptian Museum
sights.note: The vast new museum near the Pyramids, fully opened in November 2025, showing the complete Tutankhamun collection and a colossal statue of Ramesses II in the atrium.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM daily, later on some evenings

railStations.name: Ramses Station
railStations.note: Cairo's main railway station, with Egyptian National Railways trains to Alexandria (~2.5 h), Luxor and Aswan (sleeper trains leave from Giza station). Connected to Al Shohadaa metro interchange on Lines 1 and 2.
railStations.hours: Trains around the clock by timetable; metro at Al Shohadaa ~5:00 AM–~1:00 AM.

airports.name: Cairo International Airport
airports.transitNote: About 20 km northeast of downtown; no metro or rail link on this map. Taxis and ride-hailing take ~40–60 min to Tahrir depending on traffic; airport shuttle buses connect Terminals 1, 2 and 3.
airports.hours: Airport open 24 hours; taxis and ride-hailing available at all times.
